policy_title: Increase defence spending to 3% of GDP
stated: Reform UK will increase defence spending to 2.5% of national GDP by year three, then to 3% within six years, to increase the size and capacity of the armed forces, improve equipment, quality of life for personnel, and boost morale.

source.quote: Increase Defence Spending to 2.5% of National GDP by year 3, then 3% within 6 years This will increase the size and capacity of our armed forces and ensure our lead role in NATO. It will also improve equipment, quality of life for services personnel and boost morale in military communities.

bearing_set.reason: Increasing defence spending to 3% of GDP directly targets national security capacity, armed forces size, equipment, and defence posture — core O5 indicators.

The policy explicitly commits to improving 'quality of life for personnel' (job quality/conditions indicator) and expanding the size of the armed forces (employment), creating a real, concrete effect on O4 indicators for that workforce.

Moving from ~2.3% to 3% of GDP in defence spending implies a roughly £15–20bn/year increase at current GDP levels; with no funding mechanism specified, this materially worsens the funded-vs-borrowed balance and debt-path sustainability.

membership_note: Two clear non-negligible bearings: an intended improvement to national security (O5) and a real fiscal sustainability risk from substantial unfunded spending (O12). Other potential effects — e.g. defence-sector employment (O4), spending multiplier/crowding-out on growth (O13) — are either too narrow in population scope or too indirect and contested to clear the non-negligible bar separately from O12.
